## Package a version

The release command builds a ZIP locally from committed Git `HEAD`:

```bash
npm run release -- --version 0.0.0.1 --summary "Local package preview"
```

Packaging installs the selected commit's locked dependencies and builds in a temporary directory. It
preserves the source manifest and writes the ZIP, README, and metadata to
`dist/releases/<version>/`. The install archive is `qz-browser-agent-extension-<version>.zip`,
with the extension under `qz-browser-agent-extension/`. The debug archive is
`qz-browser-agent-extension-<version>.debug.zip`. Distribution and Git tags are separate maintainer steps.
Temporary Firefox loading uses `dist/extension-firefox/` from `npm run dev:firefox` and
`npm run build:firefox`. The Firefox archive is below. The split is described in
[Firefox packaging](firefox-packaging.md).

For a Chrome Web Store upload, select the `webstore` target:

```bash
npm run release -- --version 0.0.0.1 --target webstore
```

This writes `dist/releases/<version>/webstore/qz-browser-agent-extension-<version>.webstore.zip`
with `manifest.json` at the ZIP root. Upload this ZIP in the Chrome Developer Dashboard.
The Web Store target removes `key` from the packaged manifest. Source and manual packages retain
their public key to keep a stable extension ID during local development.
The manual and webstore archives use the same runtime files. The default `manual` target keeps the installation folder;
each target has its own metadata and debug archive. The Web Store ZIP contains runtime files and
licenses; its release metadata and source maps stay alongside it. Packaging checks the single root manifest,
its referenced resources, ZIP integrity, upload size, and separation of development files.

For an unsigned Firefox archive:

```bash
npm run release:firefox -- --version 0.0.0.1
```

`npm run release -- --version 0.0.0.1 --target firefox` is the same command. It compiles with
`build-extension.mjs --browser firefox`, the production path `npm run build:firefox` uses, and writes:

```text
dist/releases/<version>/firefox/qz-browser-agent-firefox-<version>.xpi
dist/releases/<version>/firefox/qz-browser-agent-firefox-<version>.debug.zip
dist/releases/<version>/firefox/version.json
```

The `.xpi` is a zip of the Firefox extension files. `manifest.json` is at the archive root, which
is the layout Add-ons Manager requires. `version.json` records `browser: "firefox"` and `geckoId`.
The package is unsigned; Add-ons Manager signs it on upload. The debug zip stays local. Chrome
`manual` and `webstore` paths are unchanged.

JavaScript bundles and embedded scripts are readable and unminified. `--no-minify` is a compatibility
no-op; the publisher has no minification pass. The Web Store target audits the extracted ZIP and
runs pinned storecheck against the ZIP. Errors, failed rules and unresolved Red Titanium/Blue Argon
warnings remove the upload ZIP. Audit reports remain beside it. See the [code audit guide](store-code-audit.md)
for dependency reductions, the exact sandbox exception, and checks that still require human review.

Use `--source worktree` to preview local edits, or `--git-ref` for another commit containing the
packaging toolchain. Scripts and dependencies come from the selected source.

Before distributing a version, obtain authorization for it, confirm the intended commit and an
unused Chrome-compatible numeric version, then run `npm ci`, `npm run doctor`, and `npm run verify:coverage`.
Package the committed source and check the output:

- `version.json` records `source: "git"` and the intended `gitCommit`.
- `target` and `packageRoot` identify the archive layout; `minification.enabled` is `false`.
- Bundling is enabled; runtime entries, readable assets, and licenses are complete.
- File counts, sizes, and SHA-256 match the package.
- The install ZIP contains compiled runtime files, licenses, and notices. Source maps are in the debug archive.

Load the ZIP's contents in an isolated Chrome profile and check the installed extension. Keep the
local `.debug.zip` with the release: it contains source maps and matching runtime hashes. Verify
those hashes before loading maps and review the source before sharing the archive.

`npm test -- release` checks deterministic output, resource integrity, obsolete-file cleanup,
license notices, and the actual readable ZIP in isolated Chrome, including formula display, offline
formula export and compressed-PDF upload/readback. Fix failures with bundling and both audit gates
enabled, then rerun the affected gates. Release corrections under a new
patch version; published artifacts and tags remain immutable.

## Dependencies and static resources

Import npm dependencies from TypeScript and pin them in the root lockfile. Ordinary dependencies are
bundled with their Chrome runtime. [vendor/assets.mjs](../scripts/vendor/assets.mjs) builds readable,
static PDF.js and MathJax resources and copies CSS, licenses and source maps. See the
[code audit guide](store-code-audit.md#readable-static-dependencies) for reviewed source transformations.

Each build records actual compiler inputs, including transitive dependencies, in
`vendor/provenance.json`. It contains package versions, upstream integrity and output hashes. Build
and release checks verify those hashes; copied CSS and licenses remain byte-for-byte upstream copies.
Reviewed engine builds record their transformations and upstream input hashes. Later bundling only
refreshes provenance for compiler-owned application files. Release
moves maps to the debug archive and removes their entries from installed provenance. See
[third-party notices](../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

For a package published without its license text, [license
supplements](../scripts/vendor/licenses/supplements.json) pin the exact version, upstream commit and
license hash. Review the supplement again when upgrading.

[Load qz in Firefox](cli.md#load-qz-in-firefox).

Browser commands start the local service and connect when needed, reusing a compatible connection
or opening the connection page once in the system default browser. When qz does not respond there,
the page offers the Chrome Web Store and a copyable connection URL; `qz connect uri` pairs a specific browser.
An incompatible service can be upgraded once before execution. The first browser is named `default`.
`status` shows the actual service address and `mcp` prints its MCP URL. The default port is 18765,
with a free-port fallback when occupied; `connect uri --port PORT` requests another port. A running
service keeps its existing address. Use the reported address when connecting another profile.

To pair a chosen browser Profile from the shell:

```bash
npm run qz -- connect uri --name work
```

Open the printed URL in that Profile and verify its online UUID with `browsers --json`.
`connect uri` prints the URL without opening a browser. `--name` sets or updates the identifier of the Profile
opening it; omit it to preserve an existing name or allocate `default`, `browser-2`, and so on.
Use `--client NAME|UUID` instead of `--name` to print the URL for a registered profile.
See [platform launch commands](cli.md#pair-a-selected-browser-from-the-shell).
Pairing is also available in **qz Settings → Advanced → CLI**.

`--client NAME|UUID` selects a browser for task and resource commands. New tasks use the first
responsive browser; existing sessions use read-only lookup, with a selection required for ambiguous
ownership. Unknown selections fail immediately; offline selections wait for the same UUID within
the connection deadline without falling back. Names are persistent and case-sensitive. End a direct-drive task with
`session cancel SESSION_ID`; disconnect one profile in its qz Settings. To release an offline name, run
`npm run qz -- browsers forget NAME`. Each command and its suggested next steps remain bound to
the resolved profile UUID.

Connections require opening a pairing URL or the settings action. Ordinary connection failures
pause after three attempts; reopen the URL in that Profile or use its settings to retry. Use the current CLI and extension together. Source edits do not
restart a working service. To update, finish current tasks, run `stop`, update and reload the extension, then run `connect`. See
[connection and upgrade details](cli.md#connect-and-stop).

`create` accepts the task text directly, with an optional title.
`--wait` follows the task across runs until its current work and accepted follow-ups and steering
messages have completed and its queues are empty; `--stream` also displays progress. Both stay
connected through questions and permission requests, then continue automatically after you respond.
Pending output includes the full request, field IDs, option values, and a submission template. Use `show TASK_ID` to
read the request again, answer fields with `submit`, continue a confirmation with
`approve`, or decline it with `reject`. Responses bind to the current wait; `--wait-id ID` selects a
specific request. `submit`, `approve`, and `reject` also accept `--wait` and `--stream`. Review the displayed
application consent notice before approving. A permission dialog the browser itself shows needs a click in the
side panel or sidebar; the CLI preserves the wait and tells you where to confirm. Respond in the side panel, the sidebar, or
another terminal while the original command keeps watching. `watch` follows an existing task with
the same completion condition. Task failure or stopping ends observation.
Task observation has no default time limit. Add `--timeout SECONDS` to set a total deadline,
including user-input pauses. Each individual connection request remains bounded (180 seconds by
default). Timeout or Ctrl-C ends watching; execute the returned `watch` recovery command with the
same task ID and browser UUID to resume observation. Observation never resends a message.
`cancel TASK_ID` stops the task.

If the selected browser has no matching task, `show` fails with `task_not_found` and exit code 1.
`watch` reports `task_deleted` and suggests listing tasks for the same browser UUID. Check the ID
and browser selection with `tasks --client CLIENT_UUID` and `browsers` before watching again.

`send TASK_ID MESSAGE` follows up on a specific task and supports the same waiting options. A busy
task queues the follow-up for its next run. Add `--steer` to deliver the message to the current run
at its next safe boundary. Both start a new run when idle; pending questions and permissions still
require a response. Streaming shows responses after the submitted message.

`data` and `images` list, export, or delete saved tables and image collections. Table exports support
`xlsx` (default) and `csv`; image collections and individual user-installed Skills export as ZIPs
through Chrome downloads. `skills` lists or searches installed Skills; `skills show NAME` reads one,
`skills read NAME PATH` reads a resource in chunks, and `skills tools -s TASK_ID` lists contributions.

# Design system

Build capability layouts with the shared tokens, `qz-*` controls, and `qz:` utilities. The Side
Panel and exported Session HTML use the same compiled skin. Begin with the [capability
guide](../src/capabilities/README.md) to register a page or renderer; this guide covers its public
styling contract.

## CSS ownership and cascade

[The default theme](../src/themes/default/index.css) declares the cascade: `theme → base → vendor →
components → utilities`. It imports [tokens](../src/themes/default/tokens.css), [base
styles](../src/themes/default/base.css), [controls](../src/themes/default/controls.css), and
[utilities](../src/themes/default/utilities.css). [sidepanel.css](../src/sidepanel/sidepanel.css)
combines the selected theme with feature styles. Feature and capability CSS stays with its owning
module; the build includes it in the complete skin.

Tokens own semantic colors, fonts, density, radii, and motion. Tailwind 4 maps them with `@theme
inline`; the build imports Tailwind utilities with the project theme. Base styles use a 13px root
font and 4px spacing units. Capability styles join the build through their own `ui.css`.

Use template utilities for ordinary layout and spacing. Shared controls, generated Markdown, complex
states, and animation belong in scoped `components` rules. Utilities can override component
defaults; keep an overridable property's hover, responsive, and disabled behavior consistent with
that cascade. Third-party styles enter through a thin `vendor` layer wrapper; retain upstream files
and licenses.

## Controls and tokens

Use native button/input semantics and the shared control states.

| Purpose | Public classes |
| --- | --- |
| Buttons | `qz-btn` with `qz-btn--primary`, `qz-btn--secondary`, `qz-btn--ghost`, or `qz-btn--danger`; sizes `qz-btn--xs/sm/lg` |
| Icon buttons | `qz-icon-btn` with `qz-icon-btn--secondary` or `qz-icon-btn--danger`; sizes `qz-icon-btn--xs/sm/md` |
| Fields | `qz-field`, `qz-field-label`, `qz-field-hint`; combine `qz-field qz-select` for selects |
| Choice inputs | `qz-checkbox`, `qz-radio`, `qz-switch`, driven by native input state |
| Result choices | `qz-choice-card` family, built with `renderResultChoice` from SDK DOM; single-column cards with a native radio or checkbox |
| Popovers and menus | `qz-popover`, `qz-menu`, `qz-menu-item` |
| Lists and decisions | `qz-list-toolbar` and `qz-decision-dialog` families; use the SDK dialog interaction |
| Scrolling | `qz-scroll`; add `qz-scroll--native` for native scrollbars |

Control overrides use the declared `--qz-control-*`, `--qz-field-*`, and `--qz-popover-*` variables.
`--qz-choice-card-text-scale` scales result-card text and line height together; it defaults to `1`.
Preserve accessible names, keyboard focus, and disabled semantics. DOM helpers and renderer
contracts are available through [SDK DOM](../src/sdk/sidepanel/dom.ts) and
[renderers](../src/sdk/sidepanel/renderers.ts).

Use `renderResultChoice(document, options)` for selectable tool results. Supply a unique `id`, the
form field `name`, a stable result `value`, and its `label`; `multiple` selects checkbox or radio
semantics. Optional `description`, short `meta` labels, an HTTP(S) `imageUrl`, and an HTTP(S) `url`
add detail. The source link sits outside the selection label so opening a source preserves the
selection. Pass `checked` and `disabled` from the owning form. The helper owns no listeners or
state; its native input events bubble to the form, which handles validation and submission.

Result cards use the theme's field, choice, and focus tokens. Keep them in one column in narrow
panels, with metadata wrapping below the title and a small optional thumbnail. Group related cards
with an accessible field label; use the existing form controls for the selection count and action.
Title, description, metadata, and source text share the 18px `--choice-card-line-height`. Separate
text blocks by 2px, cards by 8px, and use the small field padding token (8px) for card insets.

| Utility examples | Semantic source |
| --- | --- |
| `qz:bg-surface`, `qz:bg-surface-muted`, `qz:bg-surface-elevated` | `--bg-primary`, `--bg-tertiary`, `--bg-elevated` |
| `qz:text-foreground`, `qz:text-secondary`, `qz:text-muted` | `--text-primary`, `--text-secondary`, `--text-muted` |
| `qz:text-danger`, `qz:text-success`, `qz:text-warning` | `--red`, `--green`, `--orange` |
| `qz:border-border`, `qz:border-focus` | `--border`, `--border-focus` |
| `qz:font-ui`, `qz:font-code`, `qz:text-body` | `--font-sans`, `--font-mono`, `--field-font-md` |
| `qz:rounded-control`, `qz:rounded-panel`, `qz:shadow-popover` | `--control-radius`, `--radius-lg`, `--shadow-lg` |

## Template example

The `qz:` utility prefix precedes variants, as in `qz:hover:bg-surface-muted`. It is distinct from
the `qz-*` component classes. Keep semantic classes and IDs used by interaction, tests, and skins.

```html
<section class="example-panel qz:flex qz:flex-col qz:gap-2 qz:p-4 qz:bg-surface qz:rounded-panel">
  <label class="qz-field-label" for="example-name">Name</label>
  <input id="example-name" class="qz-field" dir="auto">
  <button type="button" class="qz-btn qz-btn--primary">Save</button>
</section>
```

Use localized labels in production templates. The build discovers complete class strings in HTML and
TypeScript. Enumerate dynamic states explicitly:

```ts
const tones = { ready: "qz:text-success", failed: "qz:text-danger" };
element.classList.remove(...Object.values(tones));
element.classList.add(tones[state]);
```

Use complete class names as above. For dynamic numeric values, use CSS variables in scoped rules.
Cloned templates and later `className` assignments must retain the same layout classes as the
initial template.

## Select a theme

Themes live under [src/themes/](../src/themes/README.md). To select another theme at build time,
create a sibling directory with an `index.css` and change the first import in
[sidepanel.css](../src/sidepanel/sidepanel.css):

```css
@import "../themes/custom/index.css";
```

For a variation of the default theme, the new entry can import `../default/index.css` and override
semantic tokens in `@layer theme`. An independent theme implements the same public contract. Set
`data-qingzhou-skin` on the stylesheet link in [sidepanel.html](../src/sidepanel/sidepanel.html) to
the theme's name when recording that name in HTML exports.

Keep the remaining feature imports. Each theme preserves the public semantic tokens, `qz-*`
controls, `qz:` utilities, layer order, and DOM contract described here. Rebuild using the
[development commands](commands.md); the output remains `sidepanel/sidepanel.css` and includes the
selected theme, feature styles, and enabled capability styles.

## Color schemes, direction, and export

Semantic tokens respond to `prefers-color-scheme`; the same utility class works in light and dark
mode. Use logical margins, padding, alignment, and popover anchors so the root `dir` can control
layout. Code, shortcuts, URLs, and technical inputs remain LTR; free text inputs can use
`dir="auto"`. Preserve image orientation and stored data. See [localization](localization.md) for
language behavior.

[Skin runtime](../src/sidepanel/ui/skin-runtime.ts) reads the active skin link and supplies its
complete compiled CSS to exports. Static renderers produce readable standalone content. Selectors
cover both live containers and static output, including containers styled with `display: contents`.
The panel stores its reading-size preference locally; exports use the skin's text size.

Verify relevant fixtures in both color schemes, narrow panels, RTL, keyboard/focus/disabled states,
reduced motion, and exported HTML. Use the [test guide](../tests/README.md) to select browser and
visual checks; contribution requirements, including pixel comparisons for visual migrations, live in
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).

# Firefox capability gap

This survey lists every Chrome-only or differing extension surface that a Firefox port has to
account for. The decisions from the confirmation list are now implemented in the Firefox package.
What a person or a tool result can still observe is in
[Firefox differences from Chrome](firefox-differences.md). The tables below record the API facts
that led to those decisions. They are not a description of the current Firefox package.

The Chrome package is unchanged: `src/manifest.json`, the Chrome side panel, and the Chrome
debugger path stay as they are. Firefox-only modules are omitted from the Chrome compilation.

The temporary-load package is built with
[`npm run build:firefox`](commands.md#load-temporarily-in-firefox). It writes
`dist/extension-firefox/` from the same sources. `npm run build` still writes the Chrome package
to `dist/extension/`.

Firefox facts below come from Mozilla's WebExtensions documentation and `browser-compat-data`.
Version numbers are that data's `version_added` values. `web-ext lint` on the built package
reports no errors for the Firefox rewrite that omits `background.service_worker`. Firefox
starts the event page from `background.scripts`. This checkout was not loaded through
`about:debugging`. Confirm that step on Firefox 154 or later.

## Decisions

The confirmation list is implemented. The Firefox package uses the sidebar for the workspace,
a hidden event-page frame for offscreen work, and page, capture, and `webRequest` approximations
for the debugger tools. Header initiator domains, file-access copy, shortcut links, case
recording, notification renewal, and `data_collection_permissions` are Firefox-only. The exact
remaining differences, including the debugging infobar, are in
[Firefox differences from Chrome](firefox-differences.md).

Session automations are disabled. The alarm API can take a one-minute period, which the survey
above records, and this package does not arm `qingzhou.automation.scheduler`. An event page can
be discarded, and the sidebar opens only from a user gesture, so an unattended session cannot
finish reliably. Definitions already stored for the add-on stay in `storage.local` and do not
start. The sidebar has no control that creates, edits, or runs one. `manage_sessions` automation
actions return `AUTOMATION_DISABLED`. The MCP reconnect alarm keeps its half-minute period. While
the CLI connection is enabled, a 10-second parent-API ping holds the event page across the
default idle timeout, and a discard resumes the stored connection id. That path does not start
stored automations. The guarantee is in
[MCP keepalive and reconnect](firefox-differences.md#mcp-keepalive-and-reconnect).

Chrome's manifest, permissions, side panel opener, and debugger implementation are unchanged.
The Firefox package is a second build output.

`npm run release` writes the Chrome zip. `npm run release:firefox` writes the unsigned Firefox
archive. A CI upload of that archive stays deferred at the bottom of this page.

Related pages keep their current jobs. [Commands](commands.md) lists the commands.
[Firefox differences from Chrome](firefox-differences.md) lists behavior a person can observe.
[Firefox capability gap](firefox-capability-gap.md) records the API survey. This page owns how the
two packages are separated.

The CLI daemon is outside both packages. `npm run qz` and the published `qz` command run
[`services/mcp-bridge`](../services/mcp-bridge/README.md). Load and pair steps are in
[Load qz in Firefox](cli.md#load-qz-in-firefox).

## Decision

The browser is a build-time package target. `chrome` is the default. `firefox` is the other target.
One source tree emits one package per target.

| Axis | Selector | What it chooses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser | `--browser chrome\|firefox` on [build-extension.mjs](../scripts/build-extension.mjs) | Output directory, which sources are emitted, manifest, sidebar document, sidebar skin, locale supplements |
| Product | `--product`, read by [product-profile.mjs](../scripts/product-profile.mjs) | Composition facades under `src/products/`. The default product is `public` |
| Sentence | `productText` in [product-text.ts](../src/shared/product-text.ts) | One of two strings already compiled into a shared module, chosen when that module runs |

The product axis and the browser axis compose. `npm run build -- --product public --browser firefox`
is a Firefox package of the public product. A product facade stays free of host branches. Host
behavior belongs to the Firefox adapter or to `productText`.

Edge loads the Chrome package. There is no `--browser edge` target.

`esbuild` `target: "chrome114"` is the JavaScript language floor for both packages. It is not the
browser target.

## What the build owns

`prepareBuild` accepts `chrome` or `firefox` and defaults to `chrome`. The default output is
`dist/extension/`. The Firefox output is `dist/extension-firefox/`. `--output-dir` overrides either
default. The two directories can be watched at the same time because each watcher locks its own
output.

For `firefox`, [firefox-manifest.mjs](../scripts/firefox-manifest.mjs) runs after the shared compile
and rewrites only that output:

| Rewrite | Result in `dist/extension-firefox/` |
| --- | --- |
| `firefoxManifest` | Drops `key` and `side_panel`. Drops `debugger`, `desktopCapture`, `offscreen`, and `sidePanel`. Adds `webNavigation`, `webRequest`, and `webRequestBlocking`. Sets `sidebar_action`, moves the suggested key to `_execute_sidebar_action`, and sets `background.scripts` to `background/firefox-boot.js` without `service_worker` (Firefox ignores that key). Points `action.default_icon` and `sidebar_action.default_icon` at `icons/firefox/qz-glyph.svg` and keeps the brand `icons` for about:addons. Sets `browser_specific_settings.gecko`. |
| `rewriteFirefoxSidepanelHtml` | The sidebar document loads `firefox-boot.js` and `firefox-sidebar.css`. |
| `writeFirefoxSidebarSkin` | Writes `sidepanel/firefox-sidebar.css`. That file has no twin under `src/`. |
| `rewriteFirefoxLocaleFiles` | Rewrites catalog sentences in the Firefox copy. `src/` locale sources stay on the Chrome wording. |

`src/manifest.json` stays the Chrome manifest. The Chrome output manifest matches it.

## What runtime code owns

Runtime detection chooses a sentence inside a package that the build already selected. It does not
choose permissions, entry points, or which files exist.

`firefoxExtension()` is true when `chrome.runtime.getURL("")` starts with `moz-extension:`.
`productText(chromeText, firefoxText)` returns the matching sentence. Both sentences ship in every
package, because the shared module ships in both. Use it for inline strings in shared modules.
Catalog copy that should exist in only one package goes through the locale rewrite above, so the
Chrome catalog keeps the Chrome sentence alone.

The debugger adapter gives every child frame its own session and isolated-world node registry,
including same-origin frames. Accessibility snapshots graft those frame-local trees; UID resolution
and pointer delivery return to the owning frame. Plain CSS selectors remain document-local.
Unmodified Enter on a single-line form input follows implicit submission rules. Page key events
remain synthetic, so sites that require trusted keyboard events can still reject them.

Page scripts use `userScripts.execute` in the target frame's `MAIN` world. The Firefox manifest
declares `userScripts` as optional; the tool host obtains it through the existing permission card
before the tool deadline starts. Browser-native compilation supports strict page CSP without
changing page headers. Static DOM commands and the Content bridge keep their isolated execution path.

Firefox API stand-ins install from the boot modules, which run before the shared graph:

- [background/firefox-boot.ts](../src/background/firefox-boot.ts) imports `background/firefox/host.ts`, then `background/service-worker.ts`.
- [sidepanel/firefox-boot.ts](../src/sidepanel/firefox-boot.ts) imports `sidepanel/firefox/host.ts`, then `sidepanel/sidepanel.ts`.

`installFirefoxHost` patches `sidebarAction`, notifications, offscreen, debugger, and network
hooks on the `chrome` object, then the shared service worker reads that object. It supplies
Firefox's missing `Tab.pendingUrl` through main-frame request and commit events. Request IDs keep
errors from replaced requests from clearing a newer navigation; commits, errors, no-content responses
and tab removal clear the pending field. Firefox can deliver the main-frame commit before
`onBeforeRequest`. A request whose own timestamp is at or before the commit of that same URL does
not set `pendingUrl` again, and a completed tab already showing the pending URL drops it. A newer
request, including a same-URL reload, stays pending until its own commit. This adapter uses the
package's existing permissions.
The host also sets
`qzSessionAutomationsEnabled` to false, clears `qingzhou.automation.scheduler`, and arms the
Firefox MCP wake (`qzFirefoxMcpWake`) before that service worker starts. The wake pings a parent
API while the CLI connection is enabled and registers `qingzhou-mcp-bridge-reconnect` during
event-page startup. Session automations stay disabled. The boundary is in
[MCP keepalive and reconnect](firefox-differences.md#mcp-keepalive-and-reconnect). The side panel host does the same for display capture, extension-page
URLs, and the sidebar palette, and sets the same automations flag.
`rewriteFirefoxSidepanelHtml` removes the automations tab, the new-automation button, and the
editor from the Firefox sidebar document. The
`qzFirefoxHost` and `qzFirefoxSidepanel` flags make that install run once. They are not a second
browser switch. Behavior a person can observe is in
[Session automations](firefox-differences.md#session-automations).

A runtime flag cannot be the package boundary. Firefox rejects unknown permission names at install,
and the entry script is fixed by the manifest. One manifest cannot be the Chrome package and the
Firefox package. A flag read after startup can change a sentence or patch an API the package was
allowed to call. It cannot take `sidePanel` out of a package Firefox has already refused to load,
and it cannot keep Firefox boot code out of the Chrome zip.

## Source layout

Host adapters and Firefox-only assets live in these trees:

```text
src/background/firefox-boot.ts
src/background/firefox/**
src/sidepanel/firefox-boot.ts
src/sidepanel/firefox/**
src/icons/firefox/**
```

`isFirefoxOnlySource` is that set. The Chrome compile drops those paths. The Firefox compile emits
them plus the shared graph. The Firefox build fails when a manifest toolbar or sidebar icon is
missing from the package.

`icons/firefox/qz-glyph.svg` is the toolbar and sidebar glyph: the Side Panel send-button mark
from `sidepanel.html`, scaled into a 16px box. Keep its path equal to the send mark. Firefox grants
SVG context paint only to Mozilla extensions, so `context-fill` alone draws nothing for qz. The
glyph names a fallback fill for each color scheme: `#15141a` for light and `#fbfbfe` for dark.
Firefox loads the image with the color scheme of the toolbar or sidebar that shows it.

Shared extension modules leave those paths alone. The boot files are the extension importers.
Tests may import the adapters directly. A new Firefox-only module is imported from
`background/firefox/host.ts` or `sidepanel/firefox/host.ts`, which the matching boot file already
loads.

The shared graph is the program both packages run. The Firefox package includes it on purpose:
the adapters wrap `chrome.*`, and the service worker and side panel stay the callers. There is no
Chrome-only source tree. A file with no Firefox caller would need a matching exclusion predicate
on the Firefox compile. No such file exists in this tree, so the predicate is not added here.

Production bundling inlines the service worker and the side panel, then deletes modules that only
those bundles imported. `background/firefox-boot.js` and `sidepanel/firefox-boot.js` stay outside
those bundles. Every static import they reach, except the two bundled entries, remains a file in
`dist/extension-firefox/`. The build fails if one is missing. The boot path reads alarm names from
`shared/reconnect-alarm.ts` and `shared/automation-scheduler-alarm.ts`. It does not import
`background/mcp/mcp-bridge.ts` or `background/automation/runtime.ts`, so those modules are not
loaded a second time beside the service worker.

Generated files that differ by target are written by the Firefox build step into the Firefox
output. They are not committed under `src/`, so the Chrome copy step never sees them.

`src/products/` stays a product axis. `readProductProfile` selects facades whose paths match
`{background,shared,sidepanel}/product/*.ts` and whose implementations live under
`src/products/<product>/`. Browser packaging does not read or write those ports.

### Dead weight

| Package | What it contains | What stays out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dist/extension/` | Shared sources, Chrome manifest, Chrome locales | Paths matched by `isFirefoxOnlySource`. The generated sidebar skin. Rewritten Firefox locales |
| `dist/extension-firefox/` | Shared sources, Firefox boot modules, toolbar glyph, rewritten manifest, generated skin, rewritten locales | `key`, `side_panel`, and the permission names Firefox rejects |

The path filter decides which files are copied and which modules are esbuild entries. esbuild still
follows imports from disk. On a Chrome build, a relative import or a bundled input whose path
matches `isFirefoxOnlySource` fails the build with
`Chrome package cannot import Firefox-only source …`. The Firefox build allows that import. The
boot files remain the extension importers.

`build:firefox`. Leave the variable unset for the suite's own development build.

Typecheck is repository-wide. `npm run build` and `npm run verify` typecheck Firefox sources
even though they emit the Chrome package. One TypeScript program covers both targets. Emit stays
per target.

## Release archive

`npm run release:firefox` runs `python3 scripts/publish-release.py --target firefox`. It compiles
with `build-extension.mjs --browser firefox`, the production path `npm run build:firefox` uses,
then zips those files with `manifest.json` at the archive root. The archive stays on disk.
Uploading and tagging remain separate maintainer steps. `npm run release` with no `--target`
still writes the Chrome manual zip.

```bash
npm run release:firefox -- --version 0.0.0.1
npm run release -- --version 0.0.0.1 --target firefox
```

`--version` is required, as it is for `npm run release`. Load a temporary add-on from
`dist/extension-firefox/` with **Load Temporary Add-on**. `npm run build:firefox -- --no-bundle`
forwards the extra build flag. `--browser` remains the switch that product and browser flags share
on the build command, so a product build can still pass both.

## Release artifacts

[publish-release.py](../scripts/publish-release.py) writes one archive per `--target`. With no
`--target` it compiles Chrome and writes `qz-browser-agent-extension-<version>.zip`.
`--target webstore` writes `qz-browser-agent-extension-<version>.webstore.zip`. The manual zip keeps
the public `key`. The webstore zip removes `key` and places `manifest.json` at the ZIP root. That
`key` fixes the unpacked Chrome id `ghbaodmonhcgkfeejcpffknlggbjhjgj`. `--target firefox` compiles
with `--browser firefox` and writes the unsigned `.xpi` below.

The Firefox archive is a separate directory and a separate file:

```text
dist/releases/<version>/firefox/qz-browser-agent-firefox-<version>.xpi
dist/releases/<version>/firefox/qz-browser-agent-firefox-<version>.debug.zip
dist/releases/<version>/firefox/version.json
```

The `.xpi` is a zip of the extension files, which is the layout
[Package your extension](https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/publish/package-your-extension/)
requires: `manifest.json` is a direct child of the archive, and the parent directory is omitted.
The bytes are a zip stored with an `.xpi` name. The archive contains the runtime files from the
Firefox production build, including the license notices the Chrome release packages. It omits
`.git`, source files, and `META-INF`. Add-ons Manager adds the signature on upload. The manifest
keeps `browser_specific_settings.gecko`, including id `qz-browser-agent@heleifz.github.io`, and the
Firefox permissions from `firefox-manifest.mjs`. There is no `key`. `version.json` records
`browser: "firefox"` and `geckoId`. The debug zip stays local, as the Chrome debug zip does. The
version number is the same `manifest.version` as the Chrome archive of that commit. The stores do
not share an update channel.

### Identifiers

| | Chrome | Firefox |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Id | `ghbaodmonhcgkfeejcpffknlggbjhjgj`, from `key` | `qz-browser-agent@heleifz.github.io`, from `browser_specific_settings.gecko.id` |
| Where it is set | `src/manifest.json` | `FIREFOX_GECKO_ID` in `firefox-manifest.mjs`, applied only to the Firefox output |
| Minimum browser | Chrome's own | `strict_min_version` `154.0` |
| Data collection | Chrome Web Store form | `websiteContent` and `browsingActivity` required; `locationInfo` and `bookmarksInfo` optional. `none` is not declared |

The ids are independent. `runtime.id`, `storage.local`, and update URLs belong to the browser that
loaded the package. The Firefox build deletes `key` so the Chrome id mechanism is absent from the
Firefox manifest. The gecko id is provisional until the first signed upload. A later change of that
id splits stored data and the Add-ons Manager identity. Temporary builds keep this id so profiles
created during development match the eventual listing.

## Developer workflow

CI already runs the two targets as two jobs in [ci.yml](../.github/workflows/ci.yml). The portable
job builds `dist/extension/` and runs focused Chromium contracts on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The
`firefox-package` job runs `npm run verify:firefox` on Linux. That split is the CI shape. A
matrix cell on the portable job would rebuild Chrome on each OS and still need a Linux Firefox
install, so the Firefox gate stays its own job.

Local checks follow the tiers in [Commands](commands.md). Small changes and docs run no suites;
ordinary changes run typecheck plus focused tests. When a change carries broad or browser-specific
risk, this table shows which suite covers it.

| Change at risk | Suite |
| --- | --- |
| Shared runtime, manifest, locales, content scripts, or `scripts/build-extension.mjs` | `npm run verify`; add `npm run verify:firefox` when Firefox behavior is at risk. The Firefox package compiles the shared graph |
| Chrome side panel, Playwright, e2e, release, or visual behavior | `npm run verify:chrome`. Set `QINGZHOU_PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS` for the Chrome run |
| Firefox-only trees, `scripts/firefox-manifest.mjs`, `tests/firefox/**`, `tests/unit/test-firefox-*.mjs` | `npm run verify:firefox` when the Firefox package is at risk. The Chrome package's file set does not include those sources |
| Product facades under `src/products/` | The same shared-runtime row. Product selection is orthogonal and still ships in both packages |

`npm test -- unit --match firefox` is the inner loop for adapter work. `npm test -- firefox` runs
the Firefox suite without a fresh typecheck.

A change to the Chrome emit path, including a new field inside the packaged `.qingzhou-build.json`,
is a Chrome package change. Prove the default `npm run build` output against the previous Chrome
tip when that path is edited. A Firefox-only edit leaves that output byte-identical.

## What landed

| Piece | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Build-time target, default Chrome | `--browser`, two output directories |
| Firefox manifest, boot, skin, and locale rewrite | `firefox-manifest.mjs` after the shared compile |
| Chrome exclusion of Firefox paths | `isFirefoxOnlySource` on the copy and entry list, plus a compile error when a Chrome graph still imports one |
| Runtime sentence helper | `productText` / `moz-extension:`. It chooses a sentence inside the built package |
| Product axis | `--product` and `src/products/`, orthogonal to the browser |
| `build:firefox`, `dev:firefox` | Aliases for `--browser firefox`. `npm run build` and `npm run dev` stay Chrome |
| `release:firefox` | Unsigned `.xpi` at `dist/releases/<version>/firefox/`, with `manifest.json` at the archive root |
| Build summary | The log line and `--json` stdout include `browser`. The packaged `.qingzhou-build.json` does not |
| Checks | Tiered by change size. Broad shared-graph changes run `verify`; `verify:chrome` and `verify:firefox` cover browser-specific risk. Coverage is `verify:coverage` |
| CI | The separate `firefox-package` job runs `verify:firefox`. The portable job stays an OS matrix for Chrome |
| Typecheck | One program for the repo |

## Deferred

| Piece | Why it waits |
| --- | --- |
| Signing and Add-ons Manager upload | Maintainer steps. The local `.xpi` is the unsigned file AMO signs |
| CI success upload of `dist/extension-firefox/` | The job already fails the build when Firefox tests fail. A success artifact is extra weight on the workflow |
| Gecko id confirmation | `qz-browser-agent@heleifz.github.io` stays the id until the first signed upload |
| `productText` rename | A rename rewrites shared modules and moves the Chrome package hash |
| Data-collection lists | They stay as declared. `none` stays undeclared |

# Translate qz

Keep source messages with the feature that owns them, and language packs in a capability.
Translations run locally through contributed language descriptors. The public contracts are in the
[catalog SDK](../src/sdk/shared/i18n-definition.ts) and [translation
SDK](../src/sdk/shared/i18n.ts).

## Add or change interface copy

Define a stable namespace and key with English and Simplified Chinese source text. Translate whole
sentences and preserve named parameters. For example, a feature's `messages.ts` can contain:

```ts
import { defineMessages } from "#sdk/shared/i18n-definition";

export default defineMessages("example", {
  saved: { en: "Saved {name}", "zh-CN": "已保存 {name}" },
});
```

Export that catalog as `translations` from the capability's `index.ts`. Create its translator where
the feature needs text:

```ts
import { createTranslator } from "#sdk/shared/i18n";
import messages from "./messages.js";

const t = createTranslator(messages);
label.textContent = t("saved", { name: displayName });
```

Translations are plain text. Use `textContent` or the existing HTML/attribute escaper for markup.
Preserve user data, model output, page content, imported Skill documents, model IDs, commands, enum
values, storage keys, and stored diagnostics verbatim.

Add other translations under [language catalogs](../src/capabilities/i18n/locales/), in
`<language>/<namespace>.json`. For the example above, `ja/example.json` would contain:

```json
{ "example.saved": "{name}を保存しました" }
```

Write short, idiomatic actions and sentence-case labels. English uses **chat** for a conversation,
**task** for work the agent executes, and **session** for technical runtime or authentication
contexts. Errors should explain what happened and what the user can do next. Review loading, empty,
error and success states in their actual controls; a grammatically correct label may still be
unclear or clipped.

## Add a language

Add its native name, Chrome locale, optional matching aliases, reading direction and catalog path to
[locales.ts](../src/capabilities/i18n/locales.ts). A separate capability may contribute its own
`locales` instead. Keep catalog paths inside that package. The build rejects duplicate declarations,
unknown message keys and mismatched parameters, then compiles native Chrome `_locales` resources.
Only the selected catalog is loaded at startup; missing translations retain authored fallbacks.

Use the existing regional aliases, especially for Chinese scripts. Unsupported languages fall back
to English. The language selector is generated from installed descriptors and offers **Follow
browser** alongside each native language name.

Model-facing instructions and detailed tool schemas retain maintained English and Simplified Chinese
versions; other languages fall back to English. Keep identifiers and execution behavior stable.
External Skill and MCP descriptions remain unchanged, and the model still follows the user's
requested response language.

Built-in approval cards resolve their titles and disclosures from the stored approval type in the
panel's current language. Apply this to pending and resolved history entries. Keep model-authored
questions and form labels verbatim; translation belongs to the display projection and preserves
the stored transcript.

## Preserve language and history behavior

Resolve long-lived display metadata through getters, as in the [provider
presets](../src/capabilities/models/presets.ts). The Background captures localized descriptions for
each new run; existing runs retain their language snapshot. Keep `withLanguage` within synchronous
calls; it restores the previous scope on return.

Declare canonical tool titles in `defineMessages`' `historicalLabels` option. The compiled alias
index recognizes translated titles from saved conversations and displays known titles in the current
language. Custom titles and stored snapshots remain unchanged. Use separate `Short` message keys for
compact cards and timeline labels while preserving the canonical history mapping.

Read and save preferences through the SDK. The [language settings
form](../src/capabilities/i18n/ui.ts) reloads the panel only after every participating form in the
shared settings tab has saved its current revision. Failed or cancelled saves must leave the draft
recoverable. Background tasks keep running; the reopened panel initializes with the saved language.
Chrome's extension-management labels independently follow Chrome's language, using base [manifest
messages](../src/_locales/) and contributed manifest translations.

Use `轻舟`, `輕舟` and `軽舟` for Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Japanese; other languages
use lowercase `qz`. Keep code symbols and user content unchanged. Ordinary empty chats show the
localized `core.tagline`; initial task suggestions hide it. Keep the tagline natural in each
language and preserve the suggestion's editable-draft behavior.

## Check text, layout and exports

Run the relevant catalog checks and inspect the rendered interface:

```bash
npm run build
npm test -- unit --match i18n
npm test -- unit --match language
npm test -- unit --match locales
npm test -- playwright i18n-language-settings.spec.mjs language-packs-i18n.spec.mjs tool-history-i18n.spec.mjs
```

Check both color schemes at a 320px panel width, including selected options, long labels, focus and
keyboard operation. Arabic uses RTL layout while code, URLs and technical tokens keep LTR order.
Preserve image orientation. Follow the shared [design system](design-system.md) for controls that
must accommodate longer copy. Open an exported chat offline and check its language, direction and
historical titles; exports must preserve user text and include their own display labels. The
[language workspace](../tests/browser/language-pack-workspaces.spec.mjs) and [offline
export](../tests/browser/session-export-runtime.spec.mjs) tests cover these broader surfaces.
